title: New Techniques to Route in Folded-Clos Topology Data Center Networks
problem: Data center networks require efficient routing protocols that reduce convergence time, packet loss, and control overhead during failures in folded-Clos topologies. Current BGP+ECMP approaches do not fully exploit the topology structure for improved performance.
motivation: Efficient data center routing is critical as the communications backbone supporting growing datacenter demands and must balance performance with operational simplicity.
method: MR-MTP (Multi-Root Meshed Tree Protocol) exploits folded-Clos topology (a data center network with many symmetrically arranged backup paths) by routing traffic from multiple sources simultaneously, automatically distributing load to avoid bottlenecks—unlike standard BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) with ECMP (Equal-Cost Multi-Path routing that spreads traffic equally across routes) or BGP with BFD (Bidirectional Forwarding Detection for faster failure detection). The researchers tested it on the FABRIC testbed, measuring convergence time (recovery speed after failures), packet loss, control message overhead, and blast radius (how far failure impact spreads), by deliberately injecting failures at multiple network locations.
key_novelty: Multi-Root Meshed Tree Protocol that uses folded-Clos topology's redundant paths to simplify routing and reduce convergence time (network recovery speed from failures) and control messaging overhead.
contributions: Novel MR-MTP routing protocol designed for folded-Clos data center network topologies
Comprehensive performance evaluation against BGP+ECMP variants on FABRIC testbed
Demonstration of improved convergence time, packet loss, and control overhead
Validation that topology-aware routing techniques simplify DCN protocols while improving performance

metrics.other: convergence time, packet loss, control overhead, blast radius after failures

limitations: Not discussed in abstract; evaluation limited to FABRIC testbed.
primary_theme: topology-aware routing for data center networks
